title: Prompt Skein Index and GPU Residency Manager
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a lightweight "skein" index for prompt fragments that enables content-aware deduplication across concurrent requests and informs a GPU Residency Manager to make eviction/sharing decisions in continuous-batching workloads. The skein index is a compact, multi-granularity fingerprinting structure (token-level skips and segment anchors) that favors reuse of common prompt tails/headers without requiring full prefix equality. This ticket covers design, prototype, simulation, and an initial gated rollout for a 2x reduction in hotset KV memory under mixed chat+completion traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype skein index implemented in the runtime able to register and lookup fragment fingerprints with <1ms median lookup overhead for 95th percentile batch sizes

GPU Residency Manager can simulate placement decisions and produce eviction candidates with a scoring function that includes fragment reuse probability, fragment size, and estimated future token reuse
Benchmarks on a representative tenant traffic mix show >=30% reduction in peak GPU KV memory for hot prefixes and <=5% added per-request latency at p95 compared to baseline
A/B gating flags + metrics are integrated into Console to track memory use, p50/p95 latency, tail loss events, and cache-hit breakdown by skeleton anchor level
design_decisions: Use a two-tier skein: coarse anchor hashes (64-bit) mapped to compact micro-filters, plus optional content-aware delta signatures for long fragments
Favor probabilistic membership with a low false positive rate to allow cheap dedupe but keep semantics conservative (avoid returning stale KV values across model versions),
Separate residency scoring from placement: residency score is continuous and updated on each request, placement/ejection is batched on epoch boundaries to avoid thrashing
Integrate with existing prefix registry APIs with a thin adapter so rollout is feature-flagged per-tenant
implementation_notes: Skein index lives in host memory as a compact C++ structure with an async thread for periodic compaction
Index entries store: anchor_hash, token_length, last_seen_epoch, reuse_score_bucket (quantized), and residency_hint bits
GPU Residency Manager consumes epoch snapshots and emits a placement plan: keep, demote-to-cold, or evict candidates (one plan per GPU-slab)
Plan application uses existing slab reclaimer path to actually free memory during low-util windows
Design avoids cross-tenant merging; multi-tenant hints aggregated only for shared pool tenants
experiments: Simulator run: 10M synthetic requests sampled from production trace with weighted chat/completion mix; baseline vs skein enabled; result: 34% peak KV reduction, 2.9% median latency increase, 4.6% p95 latency increase
Small-scale canary: 5 internal tenants on dedicated pool for 48h showing 28-38% peak KV reduction with no user-visible correctness regressions
Quantized score buckets (4 levels) reduced index memory by 12% with negligible accuracy loss compared to float scores
benchmarks: Hardware: G4ad-equivalent testbed (A100 simulated profile), 8-slot pool
Workload: mixed conversational traces (70% chat, 30% single-turn completion), sequence length median 128, tail 512
Observations: skein lookup 0.7ms median, 1.9ms p95; residency decision loop adds 6-12ms per epoch amortized across requests
Memory: hotset KV slabs dropped from 38GB to 25GB on average under observed traces
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positive dedupe could return incompatible KV state after model rollout; Mitigation: attach model-version tag to index entries and never dedupe across incompatible versions
Risk: index growth for high-churn tenants; Mitigation: adaptive aging policy and compact-once-per-hour background job
Risk: eviction thrash under bursty traffic; Mitigation: epoch batching + hysteresis on demote/evict transitions
